newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma land-mine blast injures four.
newsitem.headline: Burma land-mine blast injures four.

text.p: Four people were injured on Monday when a land mine believed to have been laid by Karen National Union (KNU) rebels exploded on the Burmese side of the border with Thailand, Burmese officials said.
The mine blast on the Burmese side of the Moei River, which divides the countries, near Myawadi town injured two Thais and two Burmese, the officials said.
Two of the victims were in critical condition.
The officials said they thought KNU rebels had planted the mine on the bank of the river on Sunday night before attacking soldiers at Thichahla village, about four km (2.5 miles) north of Myawadi.
Gunfire was heard until early on Monday morning, but no casualty figures were immediately available from the clash.
The KNU was formed in 1948 and is the last major ethnic guerrilla group still fighting Burma's military government.
The rebels lost all their permanent camps near the border in March 1995, and its mobile positions were overrun in a recent government offensive.

Burmese troops usually launch an annual dry season attack against the KNU guerrillas and then pull back when the rains begin in May. But they recently declared they would stay on the border as long as necessary to fight the KNU.
KNU General Secretary Mahn Sha told Reuters that if the troops remain on the border, the guerrillas will step up terrorist operations in major Burmese cities.
